Hi Tom - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

Call recap:
- Use case: in-product conversational assistant + nightly analytics jobs. Mix of low-latency chat (human-facing) and async batch scoring.
- Current traffic estimate from your side: baseline ~120M tokens/month, expected ramp to ~400M tokens/month in peak months.
- Typical prompt/response sizes you mentioned: ~80 tokens in, ~220 tokens out (avg ~300 tokens per call).

Key qualification points we promised to follow up on:
1) Budget and unit economics
   - You mentioned a ~$30k/month target for these volumes. At 120M tokens/mo that implies a target ~ $250 / 1M tokens (120 * $250 = $30k). Please confirm if $250/1M is the right target or if the budget is flexible.
2) Batching & concurrency assumptions
   - You described a continuously streaming workload for user chat (steady tail traffic across the day) plus periodic spikes during morning analytics windows.
   - From the call: average concurrency around 40 active requests, spike concurrency up to ~400 during peak processing windows; many requests are short (sub-second) and amenable to continuous batching.
   - Continuous batching expectations: micro-batch windows of 10-50ms to preserve user latency (we recommended 10-20ms for chat paths; analytics can accept larger windows).
   - Implication: continuous batching should materially improve GPU utilization and reduce unit cost vs single-request serving, but exact delta depends on your traffic shape - we'll model using your sample traces.

Action items / next steps:
- Tom: confirm the monthly baseline (120M) and peak (400M) figures and the $/1M target (is $250/1M acceptable?).
- Redwood (Camila + Marissa): will send a sample cost model + rough P&L showing how batching/concurrency assumptions change the effective $/1M. We'll attach a quick token estimate sheet.
- Schedule: propose a technical deep-dive next week (30-45m) to review traffic patterns and a short POC plan.
- Loop Legal Ops for procurement/questions on contract terms.

Attaching: acme_token_estimate.xlsx (baseline vs ramp scenarios).

If that all looks right, I'll book the deep-dive for next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

Camila - thanks for the summary and the quick turnaround. A few clarifications:

1) Volume & budget
- Baseline: yes, 120M tokens/month is our conservative number for Q4.
- Ramp: we are budgeting for an aggressive user rollout that could push to ~400M tokens/mo by mid-Q1.
- Budget: $30k/mo is the number my finance sponsor approved as a target for the baseline phase. So yes, the implied target is ~$250 / 1M tokens for the initial contract. If we can show clear savings from batching during the POC, there's room to expand the commit.

2) Latency & batching
- For chat: median p95 latency target from user action to completion is <= 400ms for primary flows. Any batching window must keep p95 under that threshold.
- For analytics batch scoring: we can tolerate minutes-long windows. The continuous-batching model for chat feels promising - happy to see concrete modeling on how batching windows (10-50ms) affect p95 and effective $/1M.

3) Next steps
- Please send a cost calc that shows: baseline (120M), ramp (400M), and a sensitivity to batching efficiency (low/med/high).
- Tech deep-dive next Wed 10am PT works for me; loop our infra lead if possible.
- Looping contracts: contracts@acmehealth.com on CC for procurement intake.

Thanks Tom - that all matches what I captured. Quick note on the cost model and how batching/concurrency effects map to unit economics (summary before the deep-dive):

Preliminary cost model (illustrative)
- Baseline (120M tokens/mo) at target $250/1M -> $30k/mo.
- Ramp (400M tokens/mo) at same $250/1M -> $100k/mo.
- Batching impact: based on similar customers, continuous batching for chat workloads with a 10-20ms micro-batch window tends to improve GPU token throughput by ~25-45% vs no batching (depends on request size and model). That can translate into 20-35% lower effective $/1M for the same latency SLOs when traffic shapes are favorable.

Concurrency notes
- Your stated avg concurrency (~40) with 400 peak is a good match for Redwood Dedicated pools. With continuous batching we typically see far higher GPU utilization for steady tails, which is where most saving comes from.
- For peak windows we recommend having burst capacity + fallback model variants (quantized) to meet p95 SLOs without overprovisioning.

What we'll bring to the deep-dive:
- Concrete cost table (baseline/ramp) with sensitivity to batching efficiency (low/med/high).
- Example latency curves for micro-batch windows (10ms/20ms/50ms) on a 8k-context model we validated on similar workloads.
- Suggested POC: 2-3 week pilot on a subset of traffic (chat path) + analytics scoring run to validate batching gain and run a production-cost calc.

I'll attach the quick cost sheet and a short POC proposal ahead of Wed. If contracts@acmehealth.com needs anything upfront, let us know and we'll route to our Legal/Finance.

Booked: Camila to send model + POC outline; deep-dive Wed 10am PT - invite to follow.

Best,
Camila
